title: EPIC: pip-installable wheels (pip install hpxpy, bundled HPX)
description: De-risked via ldd/readelf. Extension links: libhpx.so.2(13M)+libhpx_core+libhpx_iostreams+libtcmalloc_minimal+libhwloc.so.15(CUDA!)+libstdc++(GLIBCXX_3.4.31=gcc13+). APPROACH: auditwheel-bundle shared libs into hpxpy.libs/ + rpath (NOT static linking). tcmalloc already direct DT_NEEDED -> bundling it satisfies LD_PRELOAD (no preload needed in wheel). Rebuild hwloc --disable-cuda/opencl/nvml to drop GPU deps. manylinux_2_34 (glibc2.34) + install gcc13 (GLIBCXX_3.4.32 suffices; bundle libstdc++). Pre-baked HPX in cached ghcr Docker image (HPX_WITH_NETWORKING=ON, PARCELPORT_TCP=ON, MPI/LCI=OFF, MALLOC=tcmalloc, CUDA=OFF, C++20) + cibuildwheel cp310-313 x86_64 + auditwheel repair. Drop HPX::iostreams_component from CMake (unused). Relax requires-python 3.13->3.10. Wheel ~16-22MB compressed/~50-60MB installed. SCOPE: single-node CPU first; distributed/GPU via source/conda. BIGGEST RISK: gcc ABI (manylinux_2_34+gcc13+bundle libstdc++).

title: EPIC: benchmark/evidence suite (prove zero-penalty + scaling + competitive)
description: De-risked. Infra ALREADY strong: timing.hpp (hpx timer, adaptive repeats, median), cpp_baseline/diag.cpp (in-binary L0 raw-HPX / L1 wrapper ladder), bench.cpp (cross-process), benchmarks/runner.py (thread/size sweep, penalty=l1/l0, scaling), bench.yml (labeled-PR, srun --exclusive medusa). GAPS: matmul + axis_reduce + f32/i64 + broadcasting NOT laddered; no scaling for new ops; no numpy/dask compare. title: CI: dedupe push+pull_request runs (push only on main) — saves the single distributed runner

Fix ci.yml: trigger push only on main (+ tags), keep pull_request for PRs. Halves runner load, removes the stall. Workaround meanwhile: merge when mergeable==MERGEABLE (UNSTABLE ok), not when all raw checks pass.

Simpler/MPI-like, faithful to neither NumPy's global-array nor HPX's segmented-algorithm model — but a viable stepping stone or fallback if the global view proves too heavy. Decision (2026-06-09): pursue global view first; keep this to revisit. See memory hpxpy-m4-distributed.

BIGGEST RISK: runtime-dtype nb::ndarray bridge (export untyped nb::ndarray<nb::numpy> + nb::dtype; import via arr.dtype()) -> SPIKE f32 round-trip FIRST. Binary ops: same-dtype required first (raise on mismatch), defer numpy promotion to A2.4; int64 true-div / and int64+float-scalar -> raise (no silent cast). Staging: A2.1 foundation+bridge -> A2.2 core kernels -> A2.3 rest+enforce -> A2.4 promotion(optional).
close_reason: DTYPE EPIC COMPLETE: A2.1(#40) A2.2(#41) A2.3(#43) A2.4(#46). float32/int64/float64 numpy-faithful incl promotion; float64 zero-penalty preserved.

title: M4: distributed Arrays (multi-locality + collectives)
description: EPIC Phase B: distributed global-view Array (de-risked). DECISION: separate DistributedArray class (not a mode of Array — views/base_ are local), Python hpxpy.DistributedArray, explicit to_numpy(gather)/from_numpy_dist(scatter) boundary; later a factory can auto-pick local-vs-dist when num_localities>1. Storage = hpx::partitioned_vector<T,std::vector<T>> with container_layout(find_all_localities()) block partition + register_as/connect_to (AGAS). CONSOLE-DRIVES-WORKERS: segmented hpx::reduce/transform over pv iterators auto-dispatch to remote localities + action-broadcast fallback; workers passive (no Python), serve actions; reuse distributed_sum pattern (hpx::async + gil_release + all_reduce). GOTCHA: partitioned_vector<double>/<long long> PRE-REGISTERED in libhpx_partitioned_vector.so, <float> NOT -> F64/I64 dist first, float32 needs HPX_REGISTER_PARTITIONED_VECTOR(float) file (B3). BIGGEST RISK: AGAS component lifecycle vs Python GC (use-after-free) -> hold pv as shared_ptr, GIL-on-dtor, complete all futures before returning. CMake: link HPX::hpx_partitioned_vector into _core. M4a runtime already merged. Staged B1-B4.
